jp: 毎日[まいにち]学校[がっこう]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きます。
en: I go to school every day.
why: A place you travel to is marked with に (or へ).

jp: この辞書[じしょ]{は/が|wa-topic}先生[せんせい]{の|no-pronoun}です。
en: This dictionary is the teacher's.
why: The thing being described (this dictionary) is the topic, marked with は.

jp: 図書館[としょかん]{で|de-place}宿題[しゅくだい]{を|o-object}します。
en: I do my homework at the library.
why: The place where an action is carried out takes で.

jp: 誰[だれ]{が|ga-question}教室[きょうしつ]{の|no-possessive}窓[まど]{を|o-object}開[あ]けました{か|ka-question}。
en: Who opened the classroom window?
why: A question word asking for the doer is the subject, so it takes が.

jp: 試験[しけん]{は/が|wa-topic}月曜日[げつようび]{に|ni-time}あります。
en: The exam is on Monday.
why: A day of the week is a point in time, which takes に.

jp: 毎晩[まいばん]日本語[にほんご]{を|o-object}勉強[べんきょう]します。
en: I study Japanese every night.
why: The thing studied is the direct object, marked with を.

jp: 兄[あに]{は/が|wa-topic}大学生[だいがくせい]です。姉[あね]{も|mo-also}大学生[だいがくせい]です。
en: My older brother is a university student. My older sister is a university student too.
why: も adds another person to what has just been said: 'too'.

jp: 電車[でんしゃ]{で|de-means}学校[がっこう]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きます。
en: I go to school by train.
why: A vehicle used for getting somewhere is a means, marked with で.

jp: 友達[ともだち]{と|to-with}教室[きょうしつ]{で|de-place}話[はな]します。
en: I talk with a friend in the classroom.
why: The person who does the action together with you takes と.

jp: 教室[きょうしつ]{に|ni-location}学生[がくせい]{が|ga-existence}三人[さんにん]います。
en: There are three students in the classroom.
why: What exists or is present with います is marked with が.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}英語[えいご]{が|ga-stative}少[すこ]し分[わ]かります。
en: I understand a little English.
why: The thing understood with 分かる is marked with が.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{に|ni-recipient}宿題[しゅくだい]{を|o-object}出[だ]しました。
en: I handed in my homework to the teacher.
why: The person who receives the homework is the recipient, marked with に.

jp: 授業[じゅぎょう]{は/が|wa-topic}九時[くじ]{から|kara-from}十時[じゅうじ]{まで|made-until}です。
en: The class is from nine to ten o'clock.
why: The starting point of a span of time is marked with から.

jp: 昨日[きのう]{は|wa-topic}十二時[じゅうにじ]{まで|made-until}宿題[しゅくだい]{を|o-object}しました。
en: Yesterday I did my homework until twelve o'clock.
why: An action that continues up to a time takes まで.

jp: 宿題[しゅくだい]{は|wa-topic}金曜日[きんようび]{までに|madeni-deadline}出[だ]します。
en: I will hand in the homework by Friday.
why: A one-time action that must happen before a deadline takes までに.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{は/が|wa-topic}黒[くろ]いペン{で|de-means}名前[なまえ]{を|o-object}書[か]きました。
en: The teacher wrote the name with a black pen.
why: A tool used to do something is marked with で.

jp: これ{は/が|wa-topic}先生[せんせい]{の|no-possessive}本[ほん]です。
en: This is the teacher's book.
why: の joins the owner (teacher) to the thing owned (book).

jp: 昼[ひる]{は|wa-topic}パン{か|ka-or}おにぎり{を|o-object}食[た]べます。
en: At lunchtime I eat bread or a rice ball.
why: か offers a choice between two alternatives: 'A or B'.

jp: 机[つくえ]{の|no-possessive}上[うえ]{に|ni-location}本[ほん]{や|ya-list}ノート{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: There are books, notebooks and the like on the desk.
why: や lists examples from a longer, open-ended list: 'A, B and so on'.

jp: 日本語[にほんご]{を|o-object}話[はな]す{の|no-nominalizer}{は/が|wa-topic}楽[たの]しいです。
en: Speaking Japanese is fun.
why: の after a plain verb turns the action into a noun: 'speaking'.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{は|wa-topic}明日[あした]休[やす]みだ{と|to-quote}言[い]いました。
en: The teacher said that tomorrow is a day off.
why: と marks what was said, quoted before 言う.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}誰[だれ]{も|mo-total-negation}来[き]ませんでした。
en: Nobody came today.
why: A question word plus も with a negative verb means 'nobody'.

jp: 一週間[いっしゅうかん]{に|ni-frequency}二回[にかい]日本語[にほんご]{の|no-possessive}授業[じゅぎょう]{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: I have a Japanese class twice a week.
why: A unit of time plus に gives the 'per' in a frequency.

jp: 図書館[としょかん]{へ/に|ni-destination}本[ほん]{を|o-object}借[か]り{に|ni-purpose}行[い]きます。
en: I am going to the library to borrow a book.
why: The verb stem plus に states the purpose of going.

jp: 勉強[べんきょう]{が/は|ga-stative}好[す]き{に|ni-change}なりました。
en: I have come to like studying.
why: なる takes に for the state something turns into.

jp: 去年[きょねん]大学[だいがく]{に|ni-target}入[はい]りました。
en: I entered university last year.
why: 入る takes に for the place or group one enters.

jp: 学生[がくせい]たち{は|wa-topic}紙[かみ]{で|de-material}鳥[とり]{を|o-object}作[つく]りました。
en: The students made birds out of paper.
why: The material something is made from is marked with で.

jp: 風邪[かぜ]{で|de-cause}学校[がっこう]{を|o-object}休[やす]みました。
en: I was absent from school because of a cold.
why: A cause or reason for an event is marked with で.

jp: クラス{で|de-scope}田中[たなか]さん{が/は|ga-subject}一番[いちばん]若[わか]いです。
en: In the class, Mr. Tanaka is the youngest.
why: で marks the group within which a superlative holds.

jp: 宿題[しゅくだい]{は|wa-topic}一時間[いちじかん]{で|de-time-limit}終[お]わりました。
en: The homework was finished in an hour.
why: で marks the amount of time it took to finish something.

jp: 英語[えいご]{の|no-possessive}先生[せんせい]{は|wa-topic}アメリカ人[じん]です。
en: The English teacher is American.
why: の connects a noun to the noun it describes: 'English teacher'.

jp: 赤[あか]い{の|no-pronoun}{は|wa-topic}私[わたし]{の|no-possessive}ペンです。
en: The red one is my pen.
why: の after an adjective stands for the noun already known: 'the red one'.

jp: 試験[しけん]{は|wa-topic}英語[えいご]{と|to-and}数学[すうがく]{の|no-possessive}二[ふた]つです。
en: The exams are in two subjects: English and maths.
why: と gives a complete list, which fits the exact number 'two'.

jp: 英語[えいご]{も|mo-both}数学[すうがく]{も|mo-both}好[す]きじゃありません。
en: I like neither English nor maths.
why: AもBも joins two items so the verb applies to both: 'neither' with a negative.

jp: この問題[もんだい]{は/が|wa-topic}難[むずか]しいです{ね|ne-agreement}。
en: This problem is difficult, isn't it?
why: ね asks the listener to agree with a shared impression.

jp: 明日[あした]{は|wa-topic}授業[じゅぎょう]{が|ga-existence}ありません{よ|yo-assertion}。
en: There is no class tomorrow, you know.
why: よ tells the listener something they may not know yet.

jp: 田中[たなか]さん{は|wa-topic}学生[がくせい]です{か|ka-question}。
en: Is Mr. Tanaka a student?
why: か at the end turns the sentence into a question.

jp: 教室[きょうしつ]{に|ni-location}誰[だれ]{か|ka-indefinite}います{か|ka-question}。
en: Is anyone in the classroom?
why: A question word plus か means 'someone' in a yes/no question.

jp: 家[いえ]{から|kara-from}学校[がっこう]{まで|made-until}三十分[さんじゅっぷん]かかります。
en: It takes thirty minutes from home to school.
why: The starting point of a distance is marked with から.

jp: 駅[えき]{から|kara-from}学校[がっこう]{まで/に|made-until}バス{で|de-means}通[かよ]います。
en: I commute from the station to the school by bus.
why: A vehicle used for the trip is marked with で.

jp: 数学[すうがく]{は|wa-topic}英語[えいご]{より|yori-comparison}難[むずか]しいです。
en: Maths is harder than English.
why: より marks the standard that something is compared against: 'than'.

jp: 友達[ともだち]{に/から|ni-source}辞書[じしょ]{を|o-object}借[か]りました。
en: I borrowed a dictionary from a friend.
why: With 借りる, the person you borrow from takes に (or から).

jp: 毎朝[まいあさ]六時[ろくじ]{に|ni-time}起[お]きます。
en: I get up at six every morning.
why: A clock time you can point to takes に.

jp: あ、先生[せんせい]{が|ga-subject}来[き]ました。
en: Oh, the teacher has come.
why: New information about who did something is introduced with が.

jp: 毎朝[まいあさ]学校[がっこう]{の|no-possessive}前[まえ]{の|no-possessive}道[みち]{を|o-path}歩[ある]きます。
en: Every morning I walk along the road in front of the school.
why: The route you move along with 歩く is marked with を.

jp: 毎朝[まいあさ]七時[しちじ]{に|ni-time}家[いえ]{を/から|o-departure}出[で]ます。
en: Every morning I leave the house at seven.
why: The place you leave with 出る is marked with を.

jp: 教室[きょうしつ]{の|no-possessive}外[そと]{から|kara-from}子供[こども]{の|no-possessive}声[こえ]{が|ga-sense}聞[き]こえます。
en: I can hear children's voices from outside the classroom.
why: A sound that reaches you by itself with 聞こえる takes が.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{は|wa-topic}黒板[こくばん]{に|ni-target}名前[なまえ]{を|o-object}書[か]きました。
en: The teacher wrote a name on the blackboard.
why: The thing written is the direct object, marked with を.

jp: 学校[がっこう]{の|no-possessive}庭[にわ]{で|de-place}サッカー{を|o-object}しました。
en: We played soccer in the school yard.
why: で marks where an activity such as playing takes place.

jp: 山田[やまだ]さん{は|wa-topic}会社[かいしゃ]{に|ni-location}いません。
en: Ms. Yamada is not at the office.
why: The place where a person is (いる) takes に.

jp: 山田[やまだ]さん{と|to-with}宿題[しゅくだい]{を|o-object}しました。
en: I did the homework with Yamada.
why: A partner who does the action together with you takes と.

jp: 朝[あさ]早[はや]く起[お]きる{の|no-nominalizer}{は/が|wa-topic}大変[たいへん]です。
en: Getting up early in the morning is hard.
why: の turns the verb phrase 'getting up early' into a noun.

jp: 試験[しけん]{は/が|wa-topic}いつです{か|ka-question}。
en: When is the exam?
why: A question with a question word still ends with か.

jp: 授業[じゅぎょう]{は|wa-topic}八時[はちじ]半[はん]{から|kara-from}です。
en: The class starts at half past eight.
why: から marks the time something begins.

jp: 昨日[きのう]{の|no-possessive}宿題[しゅくだい]{は/が|wa-topic}簡単[かんたん]でした。
en: Yesterday's homework was easy.
why: The homework is the topic being described, so it takes は.

jp: 毎日[まいにち]母[はは]{に|ni-recipient}電話[でんわ]{を|o-object}かけます。
en: I call my mother every day.
why: The person you call is the recipient, marked with に.

jp: 田中[たなか]さん{が/は|ga-subject}来[き]ました。山田[やまだ]さん{も|mo-also}来[き]ました。
en: Tanaka came. Yamada came too.
why: も adds a second person to the same statement: 'too'.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{は|wa-topic}英語[えいご]{で|de-means}授業[じゅぎょう]{を|o-object}します。
en: The teacher gives the lesson in English.
why: The language you use to do something is marked with で.

jp: 兄[あに]{は|wa-topic}もう家[いえ]{に/へ|ni-destination}帰[かえ]りました。
en: My older brother has already gone back home.
why: The place you return to is marked with に (or へ).

jp: 昨日[きのう]、友達[ともだち]{が|ga-subject}学校[がっこう]{を|o-object}休[やす]みました。
en: A friend of mine was absent from school yesterday.
why: The person who did the action is the subject, marked with が.

jp: 土曜日[どようび]{に|ni-time}スーパー{で|de-place}アルバイト{を|o-object}します。
en: On Saturdays I work part-time at the supermarket.
why: A day of the week is a point in time, which takes に.

jp: 父[ちち]{は|wa-topic}銀行[ぎんこう]{で|de-place}働[はたら]いています。
en: My father works at a bank.
why: The place where someone works is where the activity happens: で.

jp: 会社[かいしゃ]{まで|made-until}電車[でんしゃ]{で|de-means}一時間[いちじかん]かかります。
en: It takes an hour by train to get to the office.
why: まで marks the end point of the trip: 'as far as the office'.

jp: 兄[あに]{は|wa-topic}医者[いしゃ]{に|ni-change}なりました。
en: My older brother became a doctor.
why: なる takes に for what someone becomes.

jp: 日本語[にほんご]{を/が|tai-ga-o}もっと勉強[べんきょう]したいです。
en: I want to study Japanese more.
why: With ～たい, the thing you want to do takes を or が.

jp: 妹[いもうと]{は|wa-topic}まだ漢字[かんじ]{が/を|potential-ga}読[よ]めません。
en: My younger sister still cannot read kanji.
why: A potential verb like 読める takes が (or を) for what can be read.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は|wa-topic}英語[えいご]{が|ga-stative}上手[じょうず]です。
en: My younger brother is good at English.
why: The skill someone is good at with 上手 is marked with が.

jp: 大学[だいがく]{の|no-possessive}近[ちか]く{に|ni-location}安[やす]い食堂[しょくどう]{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: There is a cheap cafeteria near the university.
why: What exists with あります is marked with が.

jp: 日本語[にほんご]{の|no-possessive}授業[じゅぎょう]{は/が|wa-topic}何時[なんじ]{から|kara-from}です{か|ka-question}。
en: What time does the Japanese class start?
why: The class is the topic of the question, marked with は.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{に|ni-recipient}メール{か|ka-or}電話[でんわ]{で|de-means}聞[き]きます。
en: I will ask the teacher by email or by phone.
why: か links two alternatives where only one is used: 'A or B'.
